Match report: Enderby scores twice as Liverpool defeat Forest in Subway Players Cup

13 hours ago

Liverpool secured a clinical 4-1 victory over Nottingham Forest in the Subway Players Cup on Wednesday evening.

By Joe Urquhart

Listen to audio version of this article

0:00 / 3:04
Instaread
Previous
Next

By beating Forest, who were reduced to 10 players early in the fixture, the Reds made it four wins out of five in the league stage.

Mia Enderby scored the first and final goals for Gareth Taylor’s side, with an effort from Beata Olsson and an own goal in between.

Liverpool began the tie on the front foot, Alice Bergstrom firing wide following a low cross from the right flank.

Forest had their own warning shot in response as Tove Almqvist stole the ball at the edge of the area and flashed an effort wide.

However, the hosts saw goalkeeper Emily Batty receive a red card just after the 10-minute mark to hand a player advantage to the visitors.

Olsson darted deep into the Forest half and got on the end of a through ball before being taken down just outside the area by the onrushing Batty.

It took the Reds little time to make the extra player count as Enderby curled a wonderful shot high into the net from a low Marie Höbinger pass to open the scoring in emphatic fashion.

Liverpool continued to dominate proceedings, though Forest still threatened on the break as Chantelle Boye-Hlorkah hit a shot wide after getting in behind the defence.

Zara Shaw was next to attempt to double the lead, but substitute stopper Georgie Ferguson was equal to it.

Ahead of the half-time break, though, Liverpool added two more goals to take complete control of the game.

Olsson produced a clever first-time finish to earn her team’s second from inside the area with a well-placed shot.

And then Enderby’s low cross into the six-yard box was inadvertently turned home by the Forest goalkeeper.

18

There was also time for Höbinger to strike the post from distance ahead of the change of ends, as she unleashed a shot from 25 yards out.

The midfielder immediately threatened again following the restart, breaking away from her marker inside the box to see a header well saved from a Natalia Ramos cross.

Substitute Izzie Breen next lined up an effort at long range from which the ball whistled wide of the post.

Enderby wasn’t to be denied a second of the night as she netted a fourth goal for Liverpool.

The striker latched on to a clever pass into the box from Höbinger, as the two combined again, and fired high into the net in fine style.

Taylor’s side remained in control of possession, though Forest did find a way onto the scoresheet in the closing stages via substitute Deanne Rose.

The forward burst into the penalty area at pace and took her shot quickly to beat Faye Kirby in the last of the action.

Team

Liverpool: Kirby, Parry (McDonald, 67), Shaw, Agrez, Woodham, Nagano (Ramos, 46), Höbinger, Trueman, Bergstrom, Olsson (Breen, 46), Enderby.

Unused subs: Laws, Ward, Kapocs, Clark, Endemann, Ireland.

Next up

The Reds return to Barclays Women’s Super League duty by hosting Chelsea on Saturday (November 21).

Kick-off at St Helens Stadium will be 12.45pm GMT and tickets can be booked here.
